triage.note: S2/ADR-027. The deployed inspector reported `build unknown`, so nobody could tell which build they were looking at, and the S2 row is explicit that a hand-set env var is the wrong fix because it goes stale on every redeploy while still reading as authoritative — 'a lying build label is worse than build unknown'. The fix injects the sha at BUILD time (Zeabur exposes ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA in the build phase only) and reads it back at runtime, which makes the honesty question mechanical: the build can hand the runtime an EMPTY file (`printf %s "$FOO"` with FOO unset), an UNEXPANDED literal (`$ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`), or a placeholder word, and every one of those must resolve to `unknown` rather than become a build label. That is what NOT_A_SHA in src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py feeds through the real resolver — `src/sec10k/web/build_id.py` is stdlib-only and imports no fastapi precisely so this case can call it for real (ADR-003: the CI jobs install nothing, `import fastapi` fails there outright). The precedence is exercised too, not asserted in prose: the build-written file outranks a hand-set GIT_SHA, GIT_SHA still answers where no build wrote a file, and a checkout with a .git still reports its own short sha. The three things no eval can run — the Zeabur build itself — are pinned as text instead: the `build_command` in zbpack.json (pinned WHOLE, the WIRE_UI argument: a check that merely ASKS whether the command mentions the variable is answerable by a command that writes the wrong thing), the .gitignore line and the not-tracked check that keep the injected file out of the repo, and /api/meta calling the shared resolver rather than growing a second copy.
triage.what_this_cannot_prove: That Zeabur's builder sets ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA, runs `build_command` in the directory the runtime later serves from, and carries the written file into the run image. No agent can run a Zeabur build. Those three fail CLOSED — BUILD_SHA absent or empty, the resolver rejects it, /api/meta reports `unknown` as it does today. A fourth does NOT fail closed and no check here can see it: if the builder CACHES the build_command layer across commits, BUILD_SHA holds a valid 7-40 hex sha from the PREVIOUS build, SHA_RE accepts it because it is a real sha, and /api/meta serves a stale label indistinguishable from a current one — the 'real but frozen' outcome the S2 row calls worse than `build unknown`. No validation can detect it: a sha cannot be interrogated about which build wrote it. This is why the S2 gate is worded 'the sha must MOVE across two redeploys, not merely exist' (ADR-027 §g, PR #31 R9/R12) — curling /api/meta once would pass while frozen.
triage.red_first: Three reds, all observed. (1) The env-var-only resolver this repo shipped, with no build_command: 8 failures — no injected sha is read at all and the zbpack/.gitignore pins are unsatisfied. (2) The naive file-first resolver that reads BUILD_SHA back without asking what is in it: 12 failures — ten values a build can produce with NO human error became build labels, truncated to twelve characters and served as identity ('$ZEABUR_GIT', '${ZEABUR_GIT', 'HEAD', 'main', 'latest', 'a1b2c3', 'zzzzzzz', 'a1b2c3d4-dir', 'a1b2 c3d4e5f', and a 41-hex near-miss). That is the red that made validation part of ADR-027's ruling rather than an implementation detail. (3) The one that paid for itself: the FIRST run of this case inside the pre-commit hook reported 18 failures on an implementation green everywhere else (16 temp-directory assertions plus the two blank-GIT_SHA ones). `git rev-parse` honours GIT_DIR from the environment and git SETS it while running a hook, so the resolver answered with the repo's HEAD while pointed at a temp directory that is not a repository — every NOT_A_SHA value 'resolved' to '17d43fc'. That blocked run's report is committed at evals/report/20260822-161040-fast.json (80/81) rather than left as an uncited dump. That is a defect in `git_sha`, not in the case: an inherited GIT_DIR in a container would equally make the deployed app report a stranger repo's sha. Fixed in `_rev_parse`, which strips GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_COMMON_DIR from the git subprocess on EVERY path including the default one — not by threading `environ` through, which was the first attempt and closed the leak only for callers that pass an explicit environ while `/api/meta` passes none (PR #31 R2 rejected that half-fix; ADR-027 §e records it).
triage.refalsified: 14 measurements against the repaired tree, each in its OWN interpreter — in-process reimport is not safe here, because a pure-reordering mutation is byte-identical in SIZE and Python's (mtime, size) bytecode cache silently serves the stale .pyc, which made an earlier harness report a dead falsifier and a red baseline at random. The tree as it stands is 0 failures in a bare shell, with an absolute GIT_INDEX_FILE exported, and with an ambient GIT_DIR exported. Mutations, all red: M1 build_command deleted (1); M2 build_command drops the ${:-} guard (1); M3 .gitignore stops ignoring BUILD_SHA (1); M4 SHA_RE relaxed to `.+` (20); M5 GIT_SHA branch skips validation (10); M6 git rev-parse promoted above both (2); M6b the same under an absolute GIT_INDEX_FILE (2 — the falsifier PR #31 R4 measured dead at 0 before `_temp_repo` was given an environment it controls); M7 GIT_SHA promoted above BUILD_SHA (2); M8 `_rev_parse` stops scrubbing (2); M8g the same under an ambient GIT_DIR (3 — R10's fix aligned the oracle with the resolver WITHOUT weakening this); M9 build_sha ignores the file (7); M10 /api/meta grows a private resolver (2); M11 `_temp_repo` cannot build a checkout (1 — the skip is reported, not silent). One measurement is deliberately NOT red: M8b, stripping GIT_DIR only and keeping the other two location vars, is 0 — see the R13 debt row.
